canvas-01.description: The map portion of Sheet 1, below the key map, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It covers the southern part of the borough on both sides of Hardenburgh Avenue, from Cleveland Street and Second Street in the west to Railroad Avenue and the Northern Railroad of New Jersey in the east, and from Highland Avenue and Madison Avenue south to Lenox Avenue. North of Hardenburgh Avenue the blocks between Cleveland, Washington, Webster, Insley, Christie and Achilles Streets are platted in long rows of narrow numbered lots with only scattered frame dwellings; a Methodist Episcopal church stands on Hardenburgh Avenue at Webster Street. A heavy diagonal line along Madison Avenue and Achilles Street separates the map from the key and index above it. South of Hardenburgh Avenue the grid of Second Street, Drury Lane, Commonwealth Avenue, First Street, Spring Lane, Ruth Lane, Blanche Lane and Adele Avenue runs down to Irving Place and Lenox Avenue, again mostly platted lots with few buildings; a Roman Catholic church stands at Hardenburgh and Commonwealth, and a concrete block works on Drury Lane. The east end, around Railroad Avenue and Serpentine Road, holds the village centre: the railroad passenger depot, post office, stores, the borough hall and fire department, a large open tract (block 23) and J. E. Collins' coal yard beside the tracks. Tenakill Brook crosses the south-east corner at the Cresskill boundary. The upper part of the page, the key map at 1,000 feet to an inch with the index, water and fire notes and legend, is outside this part.
notes: A street east of Achilles Street is lettered 'Street not named'; it lies on modern Wakelee Drive.

Renamed since: Cleveland Street is now Belmar Street, Washington Street is Palisade Boulevard, Webster Street and First Street are Stelfox Street, Highland Avenue is Ford Street, Commonwealth Avenue is Brookside Avenue, Irving Place is part of Serpentine Road, Railroad Avenue is Park Street.
Second Street south of Hardenburgh Avenue has no modern counterpart on its 1925 line.

Buildings of note: Methodist Episcopal church, Roman Catholic church, passenger depot and post office of the Northern Railroad of New Jersey, borough hall and fire department, J. E. Collins coal yard, a concrete block works.

Sheet 1. Upper third: key map of the borough at 1,000 ft to an inch, index of specials, water and fire notes and legend (not georeferenced, left out of the mask). Below the heavy line: map at 100 ft to an inch of Hardenburgh Avenue between Cleveland Street and Railroad Avenue, Highland Avenue to Lenox Avenue (Cleveland, Washington, Webster, Insley, Christie, Achilles; 2nd St, Drury Lane, Commonwealth Av, 1st St, Spring Lane, Ruth Lane, Blanche Lane, Adele Av, Irving Pl, Serpentine Rd, Railroad Av), with the N.R.R. of N.J. depot. One part.

sheet-2-1.description: The main map of Sheet 2, drawn at 100 feet to an inch inside a heavy border line. It covers the west side of the borough between Madison Avenue in the north and Lenox Avenue in the south, from Knickerbocker Road in the west to Cleveland and Second Streets in the east, with Hardenburgh Avenue crossing the middle. The numbered streets, Seventh, Sixth, Fifth, Fourth, Third and Second, run north and south between long rows of narrow numbered building lots; Fifth Street north of Hardenburgh is marked 'not opened'. North of Hardenburgh Avenue, between Fifth Street and Columbus Avenue, block 28 is an open estate with a single house named 'Shady Lawn' and a large compass rose; further east Highland Avenue runs from Columbus Avenue to Cleveland Street. Elm Street is shown entering Madison Avenue from the north. Building is sparse: frame dwellings scattered along Knickerbocker Road, Seventh Street and the blocks south of Hardenburgh Avenue, with water pipes along Hardenburgh Avenue and Seventh Street. The Haworth boundary runs along the west edge, beside the heavy line that separates this part from part 2 (Knickerbocker Road north of Madison Avenue), and Lenox Avenue at the bottom borders unmapped ground marked 'no exposure'.
notes: Renamed since: Seventh Street is Vanhorn Street, Sixth Street is Woodland Road, Fifth Street is Prescott Street, Fourth Street and Elm Street are Stewart Street, Columbus Avenue is Columbus Road, Cleveland Street is Belmar Street.
Fifth Street north of Hardenburgh Avenue is marked 'not opened'.
Shady Lawn, a house in an open block of about six acres on Hardenburgh Avenue.

100 ft to an inch. Two parts. Part 1 (inside the heavy line): Madison Avenue to Lenox Avenue, Knickerbocker Road to 2nd Street (7th to 2nd Streets, Columbus Av, Cleveland, Highland Av). Part 2 (L-shaped, outside the heavy line): Knickerbocker Road from Madison Avenue north to Prospect, drawn shifted down the left edge, with Delaware and Jefferson Avenues and the Haworth line, and Prospect from Knickerbocker to Columbus Avenue (Elm, Chestnut) along the top.

sheet-2-2.description: The L-shaped part of Sheet 2 outside the heavy border line, at 100 feet to an inch. A strip down the left edge shows Knickerbocker Road north of Madison Avenue, drawn shifted down the sheet beside the main map: blocks 39, 30, 41 and 31 between the Haworth boundary line and Knickerbocker Road, with Delaware Avenue and Jefferson Avenue running west and Jefferson Avenue east of the road, and a narrow 30 foot Seventh Street on the east side. The strip continues at the top of the sheet into a band along Prospect, from Knickerbocker Road east past Elm Street and Chestnut Street to Columbus Avenue (blocks 56 to 61), with a 6 inch water pipe from Closter along Knickerbocker Road. The area is almost entirely platted lots of 25 and 50 feet with only a handful of frame dwellings. Block 40 west of Knickerbocker Road is undeveloped, and the ground east of Columbus Avenue at the top right is marked 'no exposure'. Madison Avenue at the foot of the strip is the same street as at the head of the main map.
notes: Renamed since: Elm Street is Woodland Road, Columbus Avenue is Columbus Road; Prospect is Prospect Street.
Delaware Avenue west of Knickerbocker Road lies on the line of modern Prospect Avenue; Jefferson Avenue west of the road is modern Jefferson Avenue.
The strip is drawn displaced from its true position: it is the northward continuation of Knickerbocker Road from the head of the main map.

100 ft to an inch. Two parts. Part 1 (inside the heavy line): Madison Avenue to Lenox Avenue, Knickerbocker Road to 2nd Street (7th to 2nd Streets, Columbus Av, Cleveland, Highland Av). Part 2 (L-shaped, outside the heavy line): Knickerbocker Road from Madison Avenue north to Prospect, drawn shifted down the left edge, with Delaware and Jefferson Avenues and the Haworth line, and Prospect from Knickerbocker to Columbus Avenue (Elm, Chestnut) along the top.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the centre and east of the borough around the junction of County Road, Piermont Avenue and Hardenburgh Avenue. The Northern Railroad of New Jersey runs down the west edge, with Tenakill Brook and its dammed pond beside it. County Road runs north and south near the west side; Piermont Avenue leaves it north-east at Hardenburgh Avenue, and Hardenburgh Avenue continues east as Hardenburgh Road. North-east of Piermont Avenue the irregular streets of Orchard, Northwood and High (not open) are laid out in large lots and platted blocks (Sections 4 and 5, blocks 72 and 73); the Demarest Public School, of stone, stands on Piermont Avenue and the Demarest Baptist Church between Piermont Avenue and County Road. South of Hardenburgh Avenue are a greenhouse and nursery on block 63, a stone house on County Road, and the platted subdivision of Park, Central Avenue, Demarest Avenue (west part not open), Eastwood and Covert (not open), blocks 62 to 68 and 74, still mostly vacant. Sections 3, 7 and 8 are large undivided tracts. The Demarest and Cresskill boundary crosses the south-west corner, and the north, east and south edges are marked 'no exposure'.
notes: Renamed since: Piermont Avenue is Piermont Road; County Road south of Hardenburgh Avenue is now Piermont Road; Hardenburgh Road is part of Hardenburgh Avenue; Park is Lincoln Street; Orchard is Orchard Road; High is High Street.
Eastwood probably lies on modern Rodney Place; its junctions disagreed with the fit by 5 to 14 m and were not used.
High Street, Demarest Avenue west of Park and Covert are marked 'not open'.
Buildings of note: Demarest Public School (District No. 14), Demarest Baptist Church, a greenhouse.

100 ft to an inch. One part, irregular streets: Hardenburgh Avenue and Road, County Road, Piermont Avenue, Orchard, Northwood, High (not open), Park, Central and Demarest Avenues, Eastwood, Covert; Tenakill Brook and the Northern Railroad of New Jersey at the left edge; Demarest Baptist Church and Public School.

sheet-4-1.description: The left part of Sheet 4, at 100 feet to an inch, drawn turned on the page so that Anderson Avenue runs straight up the sheet (north points to the upper left). It covers Anderson Avenue in the south-east of the borough from Hardenburgh Road down to William Street. The land is large lots and open ground: Section 6 west of the avenue, blocks 80, 85 and 89 to the west and 88, 116, 79, 84 and 78 to the east. Small platted streets are mostly paper streets: Private Lane, Elm Road, Maclay, Tipton, Embury and William are all marked 'not open'. A brook crosses the avenue, forming a pond with an ice house on its west side; dog kennels stand on block 88 east of the avenue. Scattered frame dwellings with poultry houses and sheds line Anderson Avenue. The heavy vertical line on the right separates this part from part 2, which continues the avenue to the south; ground beyond the drawn lots on the west is marked 'no exposure'.
notes: Renamed since: Hardenburgh Road is Hardenburgh Avenue; Elm Road lies on modern Orchard Road.
Elm Road, Maclay, Tipton, Embury and William are marked 'not open'.
Buildings of note: an ice house at the pond, dog kennels.

100 ft to an inch; sheet drawn turned about 37 degrees (Anderson Avenue drawn vertical, north arrow points up-left). Two parts divided by a heavy vertical line. Part 1 (left): Anderson Avenue from Hardenburgh Road to William Street (Private Lane, Elm Road, Maclay, Tipton, Embury, all mostly not open). Part 2 (right): Anderson Avenue from William Street to County Road, County Road south to the Cresskill line (William, Edward not open). Only junctions along Anderson Avenue survive: both parts are helmert fits.

sheet-4-2.description: The right part of Sheet 4, at 100 feet to an inch, drawn turned like the rest of the sheet with Anderson Avenue running up the page. It continues Anderson Avenue southward from William Street to County Road and follows County Road south to the Borough of Cresskill line. The platted blocks 90 and 91 between William, Edward and County Road are numbered in narrow lots and are vacant except for one dwelling; William and Edward are marked 'not open'. East of Anderson Avenue and along County Road the land is in large holdings of Sections 9 and 10, with a few frame dwellings, sheds and a stone house. A brook crosses County Road and the open ground of Section 9. The sheet ends at the Demarest and Cresskill boundary with the note 'See map of Cresskill'; the margins are marked 'no exposure'.
notes: William and Edward are marked 'not open'.
'See map of Cresskill' below the south boundary.
